text: Starting on the alt-drag copy undo bug. Read finalizeAltCopy (braindump.js:2203) and the drag onEnd handler (:8975). Each stroke of a drawing is its own text node, so a multi-stroke drawing is N nodes, and finalizeAltCopy pushes N separate create actions. Building a Playwright probe to measure it.

Reproduced. Alt-dragging a 3-stroke drawing needs FOUR ctrl+z presses: three that delete the left-behind copy one stroke at a time, then a fourth that finally moves the dragged set home. Cause is finalizeAltCopy at braindump.js:2203 pushing one separate create action per clone, on top of the move action finishNodeDrag pushed a line earlier. A batch action type already exists in applyReverse, it just is not used here.

Fix proven in the browser without touching the file. Serving a patched braindump.js over route interception: alt-dragging three strokes now undoes in ONE ctrl+z instead of four, redo restores the copy in one press, and a plain drag, an alt-released-mid-drag, a zero-displacement alt-drag and two alt-drags in a row all undo in exactly one press each. The nodes array read back from the local save matches the DOM in every case. Two hunks: tag the move action while alt-copy is engaged (line 2294), and have finalizeAltCopy fold that move plus every clone create into one batch action (line 2210).
Done. Diagnosis and proven patch returned for the alt-drag copy undo bug. Server on 4221 stopped, nothing written outside .tmp/scratch/opus5-2/ and this feed file.
